findings.issue_text: [BUG] Changing the forEach callback to async (vital/lib/reschedule.ts:125) means the try/catch wrapping the forEach can no longer catch errors from the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent calls, and the returned promises are discarded. When getCalendar or calendar.deleteEvent rejects during a reschedule, the rejection escapes the try/catch as an unhandled promise rejection, the old calendar event is silently never deleted, and the subsequent reschedule steps (upserting the new event) proceed while deletions are still in flight, producing duplicate calendar events.

[BUG] Changing the forEach callback to async (wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125) means the try/catch wrapping the forEach can no longer catch errors from the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent calls, and the returned promises are discarded. A failing getCalendar or calendar.deleteEvent during reschedule becomes an unhandled rejection that bypasses the try/catch, so the old event is left on the user's calendar and the reschedule continues without waiting for deletion, causing duplicate events.

[BUG] bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...}) (bookings.tsx:553) discards the promise returned by each async callback, so neither the caller nor any surrounding error handling observes the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent results. During a reschedule via tRPC, old calendar events are deleted in fire-and-forget fashion: rejections are unhandled and the reschedule response returns before the old event's deletion completes (or fails), so users see duplicate calendar events and failures are never logged or surfaced.

[BUG] Converting appStore's values to import() promises changes the type of the exported default object to Promise-wrapped modules, but the diff only updates a subset of its consumers; any other file in the repository doing appStore[key].lib or passing appStore[key] synchronously now receives a Promise and its property access yields undefined. Out-of-diff consumers of appStore (e.g., app-installation/payment/webhook lookup paths not touched in this diff) will do `"lib" in app` against a Promise, get false, and silently treat every installed app as unimplemented — runtime feature loss with no error, e.g., payments and calendar integrations reported as not implemented.

[ADVISORY] All dynamic import() calls are invoked eagerly when the appStore module object literal is constructed, so this is not lazy loading: every app package's chunk is fetched/loaded at first import of packages/app-store, same as before. Serverless cold starts and the browser bundle still load all app packages immediately; anyone expecting the 'Async import' title to reduce cold-start footprint or only load needed apps gets no benefit — the only change is Promise indirection. If actual laziness is wanted, the values must be () => import(...) thunks.

[ADVISORY] getCalendarCredentials stores the now-Promise-returning getCalendar(credential) result in the credential objects it returns, so its return type silently changed to carry Promise<Calendar|null> in the `calendar` field while the declared shape (per its consumers) implies a resolved Calendar. Any existing caller of getCalendarCredentials outside getConnectedCalendars that reads item.calendar directly (the diff only fixes getConnectedCalendars via `await item.calendar`) gets a Promise, and property access like calendar.getBusyDates becomes undefined-function errors at booking-time; the type drift also invites future misuse.

[BUG] Changing forEach's callback to async makes the per-bookingRef deletions fire-and-forget: the promises are never awaited and the surrounding try/catch no longer captures rejections. When deleteEvent (or the dynamic import) rejects during a Vital reschedule, the rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of hitting the existing catch; the reschedule flow reports success while the old calendar event/video meeting deletion silently failed, leaving orphaned events.

[BUG] Changing forEach's callback to async makes the deletion promises unawaited and invisible to the enclosing try/catch, exactly as in the vital copy of this code. A failing deleteEvent or a rejected dynamic import during wipemycalother reschedule is swallowed as an unhandled rejection; the stale booking event is never removed from the external calendar and no error is surfaced to the caller.

[BUG] The reschedule handler's bookingRefsFiltered.forEach now uses an async callback, so the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent promises are discarded and any rejection escapes the surrounding error handling as an unhandled rejection. A user rescheduling a booking via the tRPC viewer route gets a successful response even when the external calendar event deletion fails; the error never reaches the route's error path, and orphaned events remain on the organizer's calendar.

[ADVISORY] getCalendarCredentials stores the un-awaited Promise<Calendar|null> from getCalendar into the item, deferring failure to the later `await item.calendar` in getConnectedCalendars, with no other consumers audited in this diff. Any other existing consumer of getCalendarCredentials that reads item.calendar synchronously (as getConnectedCalendars did before this diff) now receives a Promise where it expects a Calendar|undefined and will misbehave at runtime; the diff only patched the one call site it touched, so out-of-tree or in-repo callers on other branches of this data are silently broken.

[ADVISORY] The appStore object literal evaluates all 28 `import()` expressions eagerly at module-load time, so every app chunk is fetched as soon as anything imports appStore, not on first `await appStore[key]`. The stated purpose of the change (deferring app-store loading) is not achieved for the module-evaluation cost: a serverless cold start that touches appStore for one payment app still initiates network/compilation work for all 28 apps' chunks, including stripepayment, sendgrid, zoomvideo, etc.

[ADVISORY] No test in this diff covers the changed getCalendar/getVideoAdapters/appStore contract (Promise-returning), and the diff contains no test-shaped files at all despite rewriting the async semantics of booking cancellation, reschedule, and payment paths. The three fire-and-forget forEach bugs that this diff introduces (unawaited async callbacks) shipped undetected precisely because no spec exercises the deletion-error path; the next regression in this conversion (e.g. a missed await at a new call site) will likewise reach production unverified.

[BUG] Changing forEach's callback to async makes the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent chain fire-and-forget, because forEach does not await the returned promises. The surrounding try/catch no longer covers these operations, and Reschedule can resolve before calendar deleteEvent calls complete — rescheduling finishes while the old event deletion is still in flight, and a rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of being caught.

[BUG] forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...}) swallows the new awaits: forEach does not await async callbacks. The try/catch around the loop cannot catch async failures and Reschedule returns before deletions settle; errors surface as unhandled rejections and the booking is marked rescheduled while external calendar deletion may still fail silently.

[BUG] bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...}) makes the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent unawaited by the caller. The reschedule mutation returns before external calendar deletions complete; a deleteEvent failure is silently dropped (unhandled rejection) rather than failing the operation the caller sees.

[BUG] getCalendarCredentials still calls the now-async getCalendar synchronously (const calendar = getCalendar(credential)) and stores the resulting Promise<Calendar|null> in the object under a field typed as Calendar|null. Every consumer of getCalendarCredentials other than getConnectedCalendars (which was patched to `await item.calendar`) receives a Promise where the type claims Calendar|null; their `if (!calendar)` checks pass on the truthy Promise and calendar.deleteEvent(...) is called on a Promise, crashing with TypeError. The sync signature contract of getCalendarCredentials is broken while only one call site was migrated.

[BUG] credential forEach callback was made async (forEach(async ...)), so the awaited getCalendar inside is not awaited by the loop. The recurring-event deletion loop fires unawaited promises; the handler's downstream Promise.all over apiDeletes misses these deletions (they're pushed after the await inside the unawaited callback, often too late), so cancellations of recurring bookings can be reported complete before external calendar events are actually deleted, with failures unobservable.

[ADVISORY] The stated intent is async (lazy) import, but every entry eagerly executes import() at module-evaluation time, so all 29 app packages load in parallel as soon as appStore is first imported. No laziness is achieved: the change adds async plumbing and its attendant bugs (unawaited forEach, Promise-in-typed-field) while still loading every integration on any first touch of appStore, including in processes (short-lived scripts, cron workers) that need only one app. The implementation is not traceable to the stated requirement; the only real gain is parallel load.

[ADVISORY] await appStore[...] awaits a memoized import() promise with no rejection handling, so a single failing module (build artifact missing or top-level throw in any app package) poisons the shared promise. Every subsequent getCalendar call for that app rejects with the original module-load error instead of hitting the existing 'calendar of type X is not implemented' warn-and-return-null path — booking flows that previously degraded gracefully for unimplemented calendars now throw per request.

[ADVISORY] The legacy-branch deletion loop was converted from a synchronous forEach collecting parallel promises into a sequential for-of with await per credential, serializing external calendar deletions. Users cancelling pre-refactor bookings with several connected calendars now wait for each provider API call in series (each can take seconds/time out), lengthening the cancel request latency versus the prior parallel behavior for no requirement-driven reason.

[BUG] Converting the credentials forEach callback to `async` (adding `await getCalendar` inside it) defers all work in the callback body to a microtask that runs after forEach returns, so any collection the callback pushes into (apiDeletes / later-awaited promises) is read before the pushes happen. When a recurring booking is cancelled, the per-credential cleanup inside this loop executes only after the handler has already moved past the loop; if the surrounding code awaits a Promise.all over the collected deletes/updates, those entries were never pushed and the calendar cleanup API calls are silently dropped — the calendar event is never deleted while the booking is marked cancelled.

[BUG] getCalendarCredentials still calls `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` without await, so the exported shape of `calendar` in its returned items silently changed from `Calendar | null` to `Promise<Calendar | null>`. Only getConnectedCalendars was updated (via `await item.calendar`); every other out-of-diff caller of the exported getCalendarCredentials that does `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` or any method access now invokes it on a Promise, throwing TypeError, or passes a truthy Promise where the `if (!calendar)` null-check used to filter unimplemented calendar types — that filter no longer works at the point of the map.

[BUG] `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar ... })` converts previously synchronous initiation of `calendar.deleteEvent` into deferred, un-awaited work that the surrounding reschedule handler never waits for. On a reschedule, the old event deletion is now scheduled only after the dynamic import resolves and the forEach has already returned; the tRPC handler can complete (and in a serverless deployment the lambda can freeze/terminate) before the deleteEvent network call is issued, leaving stale events on the user's calendar with no error surfaced.

[BUG] `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` defers `calendar?.deleteEvent` behind an awaited dynamic import inside a callback whose return value forEach discards, so the deletion is fire-and-forget work scheduled after the loop. The reschedule flow finishes and the request may be terminated (serverless) before the deferred deleteEvent executes; previously deleteEvent was invoked synchronously during the loop, so the diff introduces a window where cancellation cleanup is lost with no logging or error.

[BUG] Same `forEach(async ...)` deferral as the vital copy: the awaited `getCalendar` pushes `calendar?.deleteEvent` invocation past the end of the loop while its promise is discarded by forEach. Reschedule cleanup deletions are scheduled after the handler continues; on serverless or process-exit paths the external delete call never fires, leaving orphaned calendar events, and any rejection is an unhandled promise rejection.

[ADVISORY] All 29 `import()` calls are evaluated eagerly at module scope, so every app package's chunk is fetched/loaded the moment appStore is imported — the dynamic imports achieve zero code-splitting or lazy-loading; they only wrap the store in promises. The stated goal of the PR (async/lazy import of appStore packages) is not met: startup still pays the full cost of loading all integrations (including payment/video/calendar SDKs), and every consumer in this diff now carries an extra `await` for no load-time benefit; a future fix should store thunks (`() => import(...)`) and await on access.

[ADVISORY] Because the import promises are created at module load and only some consumers await them, a chunk load failure or a package throwing during module initialization becomes an unhandled promise rejection at startup rather than a surfaced import error. Operators see the process crash (or, with an unhandled-rejection policy of log-only, silently degraded integrations) with no stack pointing at the failing app package, and each `await appStore[...]` site re-rejects with a bare chunk-load error that the surrounding guards (`"lib" in app`) cannot classify as 'not implemented'.

[ADVISORY] `await appStore[calendarType.split("_").join("") as keyof typeof appStore]` awaits a value that can be `undefined` for an unknown credential type, so the subsequent `"lib" in calendarApp` guard now runs against a resolved-undefined instead of a sync undefined — no behavioral change but the stringly-typed discriminator (`type` transformed by split/join) is still an untyped magic-string contract duplicated with videoClient's identical transform. The `zoom_video` -> `zoomvideo` naming convention lives in at least three hand-maintained copies (getCalendar, videoClient.getVideoAdapters, appStore keys); adding an app whose dirName doesn't match the transform breaks silently at runtime via the 'not implemented' warn path instead of at compile time, and the next maintainer adding an app must remember to update the parallel key list in index.ts.

[BUG] The dynamic imports are evaluated eagerly at module-load time, so every appStore package is still loaded synchronously-in-parallel at first import of app-store, not lazily per use. The PR's stated objective (async/lazy import of appStore packages) is not achieved: importing appStore still pulls every integration's module graph at process start (memory cost on every worker), and any app whose module-level code throws now turns a previously per-request, per-app failure into a hard startup crash for the entire server; the intent of deferring loading was silently dropped during review iteration without acceptance.

[BUG] Changing the forEach callback to async makes the `await getCalendar(...)` rejections escape the surrounding try/catch, becoming unhandled promise rejections. Previously a calendar-module import failure or deleteEvent throw was contained by the try/catch after bookingRef deletion; now the rejection fires on a later microtask, skips the catch, and surfaces as an unhandledRejection that can crash the Node process — same silent behavior change at the same line in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts.

[BUG] Changing the forEach callback to async makes the `await getCalendar(...)` rejections escape the surrounding try/catch, becoming unhandled promise rejections. A failed calendar import or deleteEvent throw inside the loop now bypasses the try/catch that previously contained it and surfaces as an unhandledRejection, crashing workers during reschedule.

[BUG] Changing the forEach callback to async makes rejections from `await getCalendar(...)` and deleteEvent escape the surrounding try block as unhandled promise rejections. A failing calendar package import or deleteEvent call during reschedule now rejects outside the try/catch, producing an unhandledRejection instead of the previously contained error path; the calls are also never awaited before the request continues, so deletions race the response.

[BUG] `forEach(async (credential) => { ... await getCalendar(credential) ... })` runs fire-and-forget: the loop neither awaits nor catches the async work. Calendar event updates for recurring-series bookings are launched but never awaited inside the request handler, so the response can be returned (and the process can exit/restart) before the external calendar mutations complete, and any rejection becomes an unhandledRejection crashing the worker — a silent change from previously synchronous, error-contained iteration.

[ADVISORY] getCalendarCredentials now stores `const calendar = getCalendar(credential)` — an unresolved Promise — in the items it returns while the function's exported shape still reads as `{ calendar: Calendar | null }` to every non-updated consumer. Only getConnectedCalendars (updated in this diff to `await item.calendar`) honors the new Promise contract; any other existing caller of getCalendarCredentials that does a truthiness check or uses `item.calendar.deleteEvent` directly now operates on a Promise object (always truthy, no methods), so hidden out-of-diff call sites silently no-op or throw — the type contract was changed without a signature change flagging it.

[BUG] forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...}) launches the async callbacks without awaiting them, so the deleteEvent/getCalendar work is fire-and-forget and any rejection from the now-async dynamic import or calendar deletion becomes an unhandled promise rejection. A failed dynamic import or thrown error inside the callback is no longer surfaced; the reschedule handler proceeds (and the surrounding try/catch never fires because the promise is discarded), leaving orphaned external calendar events undeleted while the booking is treated as rescheduled, plus potential process-level unhandledRejection crashes.

[BUG] forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...}) discards the async callbacks' promises, so deletions are fire-and-forget and rejections (now possible because getCalendar awaits a dynamic import) escape the surrounding try/catch entirely. External calendar events are left undeleted while the reschedule is reported as successful, and import/deletion errors surface as unhandled promise rejections instead of being caught by the try block two lines below.

[BUG] Changing forEach((bookingRef) => {...}) to forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...}) makes the callback's promise (including the awaited getCalendar and deleteEvent) unobserved by the enclosing handler. The deleteEvent calls for calendar references race ahead of the handler's remaining logic and any failure inside the awaited dynamic import is swallowed as an unhandled rejection, so calendar events can remain on external providers after a reschedule the system records as complete.

[BUG] getCalendarCredentials still calls the now-async getCalendar synchronously (`const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` with no await) and stuffs the resulting Promise<Calendar|null> into the `calendar` field of the returned objects, a silent type change on this function's public shape that is only papered over by the single consumer updated in this diff (getConnectedCalendars now does `await item.calendar`). Any other caller of getCalendarCredentials outside this diff receives a Promise where the type still declares Calendar|null, so `calendar.someMethod()` throws TypeError (e.g., calendar.deleteEvent is undefined) and calendar-based operations silently no-op or 500 instead of performing the integration call.

[ADVISORY] All dynamic imports are started eagerly at module-evaluation time (`applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")` etc.), so the promise for every app's module begins resolving the moment anything imports appStore, and a module with a top-level failure rejects its promise before any guard runs. Operators lose the intended lazy-loading benefit (all ~28 app packages load at startup in every process), and any app package that fails its top-level evaluation now breaks every request touching appStore for that app with an opaque rejected-promise error rather than the previous synchronous module-load failure at boot where it was at least attributable.

[BUG] The forEach callback is now async but its returned promise is discarded, so the awaited deleteEvent/getCalendar work is never awaited by the caller and rejections become unhandled promise rejections outside the try/catch that was written to catch them. During a Vital reschedule, old calendar events/video meetings are deleted fire-and-forget; if getCalendar or deleteEvent rejects, the surrounding try/catch no longer catches it (the error surfaces as an unhandledRejection or is swallowed), so the reschedule reports success while the old event remains on the external calendar.

[BUG] The forEach callback is now async but its promise is dropped by forEach, converting the previously-synchronous (catchable) loop body into unawaited, un-caught async work. Old booking events on external calendars are deleted without any caller awaiting completion or errors; a failing deleteEvent leaves the stale event in place while the reschedule completes successfully, and the enclosing try/catch cannot see the rejection.

[BUG] bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...}) discards the async callback's promise, so the awaited getCalendar and subsequent deleteEvent calls run detached from the resolver procedure with no error handler. The reschedule mutation resolves and returns before old calendar events are actually deleted; a rejection inside the callback is never caught (the surrounding code has no try/catch for it), producing unhandledRejection and leaving ghost events on the user's calendar while the API reports success.

[BUG] The recurring-booking branch uses forEach(async (credential) => {...}) so the awaited getCalendar and the per-booking updateEvent calls inside are fire-and-forget with no rejection handler and no completion barrier. The cancellation request finishes (HTTP response sent) before the recurring events are actually updated on external calendars; any updateEvent failure is silently lost as an unhandled rejection, leaving recurring events undeleted while the booking appears cancelled.

[ADVISORY] The not-implemented warning interpolates the whole paymentApp object (`of type ${paymentApp}`) instead of the app dirName/type, so the log prints '[object Object]' or the module namespace. An operator debugging why a payment refund/delete silently no-ops gets a log line that misdescribes which app failed to load, sending the debugging in the wrong direction.

[ADVISORY] appStore now eagerly calls import() for all ~29 app modules at module-load time, so any app package whose top-level module throws (bad import, circular init, missing optional dependency) causes a rejected promise stored in the store that rejects at first await, and all modules load at startup negating lazy import except for code-splitting of un-awaited ones. A single broken app package (e.g. an installed-by-default app with a broken top-level side effect) turns every getCalendar/payment call for unrelated apps into an unhandled rejection at that await site; startup also loses the isolation previously given by loading only needed apps.

goldens.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

Operators lose the intended lazy-loading benefit (all ~28 app packages load at startup in every process), and any app package that fails its top-level evaluation now breaks every request touching appStore for that app with an opaque rejected-promise error rather than the previous synchronous module-load failure at boot where it was at least attributable.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, each entry is assigned as `foo: import("./foo")`, which *invokes* the dynamic import immediately at module evaluation time. That means importing `appStore` starts loading all app modules eagerly (no true lazy loading). Additionally, callers now do `await appStore[key]` (e.g. `getCalendar.ts`, `videoClient.ts`, payment handlers) without a surrounding try/catch; if a module’s top-level evaluation rejects, the `await` will throw at runtime rather than failing synchronously when `app-store/index.ts` is loaded. This is a real, diff-grounded performance/architecture and error-surface concern, though not a guaranteed functional defect absent a failing module.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, the store is changed from static imports to an object literal that immediately evaluates `import("./...")` for every app at module-load time (e.g. `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar"), ...`). These promises are created without awaiting or attaching `.catch()`. If any app’s top-level module fails to load, that `import()` promise can reject while no handler is attached, which can trigger an unhandled promise rejection before the first later `await appStore[...]` (as added in `getCalendar`, payment, and video code). This is a concrete runtime failure mode introduced by the diff, and it also removes the prior behavior of only loading the apps that are actually used.
